main.title: Dishonored
main.subtitle: Arkane builds Dunwall around different approaches
main.summary: Dishonored lets Corvo combine stealth, combat, supernatural powers and nonlethal solutions in the city of Dunwall.

cards.heading: Arkane builds Dunwall around different approaches
cards.text: Dishonored was released on October 9, 2012. In Arkane Studios' city of Dunwall, Corvo can approach objectives through combat, stealth, vertical routes, supernatural powers or nonlethal solutions. Tools can be combined in different ways, and the world reacts to the player's actions. Its interconnected systems and spaces make it an example of the immersive sim.

cards.heading: Blink opens routes across rooftops and ledges
cards.text: Blink lets Corvo move a short distance through supernatural means. Ledges, rooftops and openings become possible routes, allowing the player to approach a guarded area from another direction instead of waiting to pass through the same corridor. The ability works with Dunwall's vertical level design, making the choice of route part of avoiding encounters.

cards.heading: Viktor Antonov and Sébastien Mitton shape Dunwall
cards.text: Viktor Antonov and Sébastien Mitton's visual work connects Dunwall's buildings to its industry, energy production and social hierarchies. Places associated with power differ from spaces where people struggle to survive. Protection, surveillance and neglect are visible through the environments, and access, obstacles and risks help communicate the city's divisions as Corvo moves through it.

cards.heading: Nonlethal choices and the chaos system
cards.text: Dishonored offers nonlethal solutions for its main targets, but avoiding a killing can still have unsettling consequences. Players must consider what happens to a target and who benefits from the outcome. Violence also contributes to the chaos system, affecting the state of the world and later developments. Choosing an effective solution therefore means considering its consequences beyond the immediate objective.

cards.heading: Combining possession, time manipulation and gadgets
cards.text: Possession can let Corvo enter an animal's body and use a passage he could not normally cross. Time manipulation changes the relationship between danger, movement and reaction. These powers can be combined with weapons, gadgets and the geometry of a level. At GDC, the team described spaces designed to encourage combinations and emergent behavior. Tools are not restricted to a single predetermined solution, leaving room for experimentation.

main.title: Bravely Default
main.subtitle: A new role-playing world begins with Flying Fairy
main.summary: Bravely Default, known in Japan as Bravely Default: Flying Fairy, is a 2012 role-playing video game developed by Silicon Studio and published by Square Enix for the Nintendo 3DS.

cards.heading: A new role-playing world begins with Flying Fairy
cards.text: Silicon Studio developed Bravely Default: Flying Fairy for Nintendo 3DS, published by Square Enix in Japan in 2012. The expanded For the Sequel edition followed in 2013 and formed the basis of the international Bravely Default release. Its turn-based battles and job system let players combine abilities, while options adjust battle speed and encounter frequency.

cards.heading: Four companions seek to restore the crystals
cards.text: Bravely Default is set in the world of Luxendarc, which is kept in balance by four elemental crystals protected by the Crystal Orthodoxy, a religious group with influence across the world. The story follows the adventures of four protagonists: Tiz Arrior, the sole survivor from a destroyed village caused by the crystals' blight; Agnès Oblige, vestal of the Wind Crystal, who was forced out of her duties after the crystals were consumed by darkness; Ringabel, an amnesiac wanderer trying to uncover the secrets of a mysterious journal in his possession; and Edea Lee, a defector from a large army bent on capturing Agnès. Together, the party aims to reclaim the four crystals from the darkness and confront a greater evil along the way.

cards.heading: A new identity grows from Final Fantasy
cards.text: Starting development as an action role-playing sequel to Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light, it retained elements from the Final Fantasy series while having its own story and gameplay elements. The producer of The 4 Heroes of Light, Tomoya Asano, returned to produce Bravely Default. The story's writer was Naotaka Hayashi, who was brought in from 5pb. due to his work on Steins;Gate. The characters designs were handled by multiple artists, including art director Akihiko Yoshida and manga artist Atsushi Ōkubo. The game was influenced by western video games and television series, and individual elements were inspired by aspects of the Dragon Quest series and Higurashi When They Cry. The music, composed by Revo of Sound Horizon, was intended to evoke the feelings of classic series such as Dragon Quest and SaGa.

main.title: Medal of Honor: Warfighter
main.subtitle: Tier 1 operators return in Warfighter
main.summary: Medal of Honor: Warfighter is a first-person shooter game developed by Danger Close Games and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: Tier 1 operators return in Warfighter
cards.text:
Medal of Honor: Warfighter is a first-person shooter game developed by Danger Close Games and published by Electronic Arts. It is a sequel to Medal of Honor (2010) and is the fourteenth installment in the Medal of Honor video game series. The game's single-player campaign picks up where the previous entry left off, as it follows the Navy SEALs from the previous game's AFO Neptune.

Development of the sequel began after the 2010 reboot was commercially successful. During development, Naval Special Warfare Development Group (DEVGRU) members who worked as consultants for the game were disciplined for releasing classified information. The title was announced on February 23, 2012, and was released in October 2012 on Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360.

cards.heading: Campaign missions cross borders and timelines
cards.text:
The gameplay in Warfighter features different aspects than its predecessor. Features from the previous game such as peek and lean, requesting ammunition (now unlimited), and sliding returned. New features in the campaign like the Dynamic Door Breach and environmental destruction have been added.

The single-player campaign follows the story of Tier 1 operators from US Special Operations Forces and features various locations including Bosnia, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Somalia. The player primarily plays as "Preacher" of Task Force Blackbird and "Stump" of Task Force Mako. Campaign levels follow a nonlinear path and depict missions which occur at various points in time.

cards.heading: Special forces meet in multiplayer
cards.text: Danger Close developed multiplayer using Frostbite 2. Players choose among twelve special-forces units from ten nations, then select a class such as Sniper, Assaulter or Point Man. Each class brings its own abilities and equipment. These national units and classes belong to multiplayer rather than the single-player campaign.

cards.heading: Djawadi and Linkin Park shape the soundtrack
cards.text: The music for Warfighter was composed by Ramin Djawadi, who also composed the music for Medal of Honor (2010). The official soundtrack was released on September 25, 2012, on iTunes and Amazon, nearly one month before the release of the game. The soundtrack consists of 21 tracks, 2 of which were composed by Mike Shinoda, the co-vocalist and rapper of Linkin Park. Linkin Park's song "Castle of Glass" from their album Living Things serves as the end credits song for Warfighter, and variations of the song appear on the soundtrack. Themes from the previous game reappear as well, albeit in slightly differed forms. The official video was released on October 10, 2012.

main.title: Forza Horizon
main.subtitle: A Colorado festival opens the road
main.summary: Forza Horizon is a 2012 racing video game developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios for the Xbox 360 on 23 October 2012.

cards.heading: The Horizon Festival opens Colorado roads
cards.text: Forza Horizon is a 2012 racing video game developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios for the Xbox 360 on 23 October 2012. The game is the fifth instalment of the Forza series, having originally spun-off from Turn 10 Studios-developed Forza Motorsport titles. Taking place during the fictitious Horizon Festival, a street racing event, the player's aim is to progress via winning races, while also increasing their popularity level by performing stunts and activities. Unlike previous games in the Forza series, Forza Horizon takes place in an open world that players can explore.

cards.heading: Street races, skill chains and showcase events
cards.text: The Colorado-inspired map connects circuits, point-to-point events and other races across public roads. Drivers can challenge a passing rival to a race from their current position. Drifts, jumps and other driving feats build popularity and can be chained into combos. Rising popularity unlocks showcase events against vehicles such as aircraft, giving progression another form alongside conventional race wins.

cards.heading: Buying, upgrading and painting cars
cards.text: Other aspects of game-play include an auto-show, in which the player can buy or sell cars; a garage, in which the player can manually or automatically upgrade their cars, and a paint shop, in which players can create custom paints, liveries, and paint presets for their vehicles. When free-roaming, the player may encounter discount signs which, when smashed, give a price reduction on all upgrades from that point forwards.

main.title: Hotline Miami
main.subtitle: Masks, violence and an electronic soundtrack
main.summary: Hotline Miami is a 2012 top-down shooter game developed by Dennaton Games and published by Devolver Digital.

cards.heading: Miami behind an animal mask
cards.text: Dennaton Games developed Hotline Miami, published by Devolver Digital in 2012. The unnamed protagonist, commonly called Jacket, carries out attacks against the Russian mafia in a distorted version of Miami in 1989. Each top-down stage asks the player to eliminate its enemies, with animal masks granting different abilities. The story increasingly questions the protagonist's perception and his actions.

cards.heading: Two creators and an electronic soundtrack
cards.text: The game was developed over the course of nine months as the first commercial release of Dennaton Games, a duo composed of developers Jonatan Söderström and Dennis Wedin. Söderström programmed the game and wrote the narrative, while Wedin designed the graphics. Several artists contributed to the soundtrack, which combines many music genres, including electronic, techno, vaporwave, and synthwave. Hotline Miami was released in October 2012 for Windows, followed by versions for OS X, Linux, PlayStation 3, and PlayStation Vita in 2013, and a PlayStation 4 port in 2014.

cards.heading: The influence of an independent game
cards.text: Hotline Miami has been frequently considered one of the greatest video games, as well as one of the most influential indie games. Initial reviews highlighted its gameplay, soundtrack, and atmosphere, though some criticized its controls. The themes and storytelling were also praised. It was nominated for several awards and sold 1.5 million copies by May 2015. The game inspired multiple developers and contributed to a rise in indie game releases throughout the 2010s; it also contributed to the success of its publisher and the popularity of the synthwave music genre. A sequel, Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, was released in March 2015. The series went on to spawn a franchise, with two compilations of both games on platforms such as the Nintendo Switch, a comic book spinoff, and several fan games.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2012
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2012 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Assassin's Creed III
main.subtitle: A new Assassin in Revolutionary America
main.summary: Assassin's Creed III is a 2012 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: A new Assassin in Revolutionary America
cards.text: Assassin's Creed III is a 2012 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the fifth major installment in the Assassin's Creed series, and a direct sequel to 2011's Assassin's Creed Revelations. The game was released worldwide for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, beginning in North America on October 30, 2012, with a Wii U and Microsoft Windows release in November 2012. A remastered version of the game was released in 2019 for Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Nintendo Switch, and in 2021 for Google Stadia.

cards.heading: Two lives across a colonial conflict
cards.text: The game's plot is set in a fictional history of real-world events and follows the millennia-old struggle between the Assassins, who fight to preserve peace and free will, and the Templars, who desire peace through control. The framing story is set in the 21st century and features series protagonist Desmond Miles using a machine known as the Animus to relive the memories of his ancestors and find a way to avert the 2012 apocalypse. The main narrative is set in 18th-century Colonial America from 1754 to 1783, and follows two characters whose stories are interconnected: Haytham Kenway, a British Templar who attempts to build a presence for his Order in the colonies during the French and Indian War; and Ratonhnhaké:ton / Connor, Haytham's half-Mohawk son, who becomes an Assassin to protect his people and avenge his mother's death, and battles the Templars' attempts to influence the outcome of the American Revolution.

cards.heading: The wilderness changes movement and combat
cards.text: Free running has been simplified to allow for more fluid parkour in the cities and wilderness, such as climbing and running on trees, mountains, cliffs, etc. Close combat has been modified, allowing Connor to dual-wield weapons and take down multiple opponents at once, and players no longer need to manage the lock-on mechanic. Connor has access to a wide range of weapons which include muskets, swords, pistols, native weapons such as the tomahawk and bow and arrow, the Rope Dart (used to pull foes or hang them from above), and the Assassins' signature Hidden Blades. Human shields can be used against firing lines of enemies. Medicine is no longer used as health recovers automatically. Stealth is revamped, allowing players to use natural elements such as tall grass and trees to hide, along with the ability to blend between any two people.

cards.heading: The Aquila opens a naval frontier
cards.text: Assassin's Creed III introduces naval gameplay to the series. During the main story, Connor captains a brig, the Aquila, and is given the opportunity to upgrade it with improved weapons and hull armor. Control of the ship relies on environmental factors such as wind direction and speed, local presence of storms, high waves, and rocks. Engagements are by cannon, with broadsides covering both flanks of the ship, swivel guns that can be used to damage smaller ships which can be boarded to find treasure, and chain shots that can instantly take down the masts of larger ships and disable them. The Aquila is usable only during a few main story missions and a series of dedicated side missions.

main.title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted
main.subtitle: Criterion returns Most Wanted to an open city
main.summary: Need for Speed: Most Wanted is a 2012 racing game developed by Criterion Games and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: Criterion returns Most Wanted to an open city
cards.text: Need for Speed: Most Wanted is a 2012 racing game developed by Criterion Games and published by Electronic Arts. Most Wanted is the nineteenth title in the Need for Speed series and was released worldwide for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PlayStation Vita, iOS and Android, beginning in North America in 2012. A Wii U version, under the title Need for Speed: Most Wanted U, was released in 2013. Like its predecessor, 2010's Hot Pursuit, the game is a revival of the original 2005 Most Wanted title.

cards.heading: Races and police pursuits shape Fairhaven
cards.text: Fairhaven hosts Sprint, Circuit and Speed Run events, alongside Ambush races that begin with the player surrounded by police. Pursuits use police vehicles and tactics to stop the car. Defeating one of ten Most Wanted rivals adds their vehicle to the roster, giving the open-city competition a series of targets.

cards.heading: Autolog makes competition part of the world
cards.text: The game uses Autolog, the competition-between-friends system developed by Criterion for Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit, and since used in other titles in the Need for Speed series. Autolog in Most Wanted plays a larger role and gives more information to players. Activities in-game allow players to earn Speed Points which can boost players up on the Most Wanted list. Autolog recommendations have now been integrated into the game world, rather than sit externally on the menu system. Most Wanted features a new social system called Cloudcompete, which strings together Most Wanted across all platforms in an inspired example of cross-compatibility. One profile is used for all versions of the game, allowing the player to rank up on one format and continue progress on another.

main.title: Tales of Xillia 2
main.subtitle: A family can decide the fate of another world
main.summary: Tales of Xillia 2 is Bandai Namco's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 1 November 2012. Ludger Will Kresnik becomes involved in the destruction of parallel dimensions, using a family ability that gives him access to worlds whose continued existence has consequences elsewhere. Characters and places from the earlier game return around this new protagonist. The premise turns a familiar sequel journey into a problem of choices, asking what responsibility belongs to somebody whose actions can determine which version of a life is allowed to continue.

cards.heading: A family can decide the fate of another world
cards.text: Tales of Xillia 2 is Bandai Namco's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 1 November 2012. Ludger Will Kresnik becomes involved in the destruction of parallel dimensions, using a family ability that gives him access to worlds whose continued existence has consequences elsewhere. Characters and places from the earlier game return around this new protagonist. The premise turns a familiar sequel journey into a problem of choices, asking what responsibility belongs to somebody whose actions can determine which version of a life is allowed to continue.

cards.heading: A new protagonist changes the party's rhythm
cards.text: Exploration connects towns, conversations and encounters with visible enemies, while battles move the party into a separate action space. Returning companions bring their own histories into the group, and voiced skits allow those relationships to develop between major events. Ludger's role gives the player another way to approach the combat while the broader linking structure remains recognisable. The journey therefore combines familiarity with a new centre of attention. Known people become companions to somebody else, allowing their previous experiences to sit beside the problems introduced by the Kresnik family and its unusual power.

cards.heading: A direct continuation with a different question
cards.text: Kenji Anabuki and Asana Inoki directed, with Hideo Baba producing and Motoi Sakuraba composing the score. Character designs again draw on Kōsuke Fujishima and Mutsumi Inomata, with Daigo Okumura contributing to the cast. North American and European editions followed in August 2014. The game's theme places choice at the centre of the future being constructed. Its sequel structure supports that idea by returning to a world the player may already value, then presenting alternative versions whose people and relationships make a decision harder to treat as an abstract solution.

main.title: Halo 4
main.subtitle: 343 Industries inherits Master Chief's story
main.summary: 343 Industries continues Master Chief's journey on Requiem, where Cortana's rampancy and new Promethean enemies shape the campaign.

cards.heading: The first Halo from 343 Industries
cards.text: Halo 4 reached Xbox 360 on November 6, 2012. The first main game developed entirely by 343 Industries sends Master Chief and Cortana to the artificial world Requiem. Promethean enemies introduce new combat priorities, while Cortana's rampancy threatens a partnership that had guided the earlier games.

cards.heading: Building 343 Industries
cards.text: Microsoft built 343 Industries to continue Halo after Bungie. Veterans of the series worked alongside new specialists on its weapons, spaces, technology and story. Halo 4 became the studio's first full main entry, testing how familiar combat could support a new direction for Chief.

cards.heading: Requiem and the Forerunners
cards.text: Requiem places monumental Forerunner structures among forests, cliffs and other natural surfaces. Geometric lights and artificial materials distinguish the ancient technology, while bridges and large openings help guide movement. The contrast gives the player landmarks within environments whose scale often dwarfs Chief.

cards.heading: Master Chief and Cortana
cards.text: Cortana's rampancy disrupts the confidence of the familiar guiding voice. Conversations and pauses give Chief more room to respond to a danger his weapons cannot resolve. The relationship between the soldier and AI carries much of the campaign's personal conflict.

cards.heading: The Promethean battlefield
cards.text: Promethean Knights, Crawlers and Watchers fill different roles. Watchers can protect or restore other units, changing which threat the player should remove first. Knights combine mobility with resilience, while the new weapons add distinct forms and feedback to the established use of shields, grenades and interchangeable firearms.

cards.heading: Neil Davidge's new score
cards.text: Neil Davidge takes the main scoring role after the series' close association with Martin O'Donnell and Michael Salvatori. Choir and orchestral passages mix with electronic textures to accompany Requiem and Chief's relationship with Cortana. The changed sound helps distinguish 343 Industries' entry.

cards.heading: Spartan Ops, one episode at a time
cards.text: Spartan Ops delivers cooperative missions in episodes, following the UNSC Infinity and its Spartans. Narrative sequences accompany the playable assignments, with a weekly schedule encouraging groups to return. The mode extends the campaign's combat into a separate ongoing story.
